attributes.description: Alerts when the 95th percentile of upstream response time ($upstream_response_time) exceeds 1 second per host over 15 minutes, for proxied requests where NGINX connected to the backend. Requires the extended NGINX log format with timing fields.
attributes.name: [Nginx OTel] High P95 upstream response time

investigation_guide.blob:
## NGINX high P95 upstream response time

### What fired
The 95th percentile of upstream response time (`nginx.upstream.response.duration`, from `$upstream_response_time`) exceeded 1 s over the window (min 20 proxied requests). Attempts where NGINX could not connect to the backend are excluded; for retried requests only the final attempt counts.

### Why it matters
The backends behind NGINX are slow to respond, which adds directly to the latency clients see.

### Triage
1. Open the Latency section of the Request Health dashboard and check the upstream time breakdown: connect time points to network, TLS or saturated backends; time to first byte points to slow backend processing.
2. Check the slowest URL paths table (Upstream P95 column) for the affected endpoints.
3. Check the health and load of the upstream application.

### Remediation
- Scale or fix the slow backend; review upstream keepalive and timeouts.

### Tuning
- 1 s threshold; set it to your backend's expected response time.
